exposure: Management strategy for preterm premature rupture of membranes (pPROM), comparing an interventionist approach based on C-reactive protein (CRP) levels (Group A) with a less interventionist approach following national recommendations (Group B).
cohort: The study included 169 singleton pregnancies with preterm premature rupture of membranes (pPROM) before 32 weeks of amenorrhea.
finding: A less interventionist pPROM management strategy (Group B) was associated with higher rates of early-onset neonatal infection, positive neonatal blood cultures, and histological chorioamnionitis, but also with lower odds of fetal death, while severe neonatal morbidity was primarily influenced by lower birth weight.
birth_weight: Lower birth weight was identified as a significant independent predictor of severe neonatal morbidity.
gest_age: The study included pregnancies with pPROM before 32 weeks of amenorrhea, and gestational age at birth was not an independent predictor of severe neonatal morbidity.
